name: Rimac Nevera
notes: Rimac Nevera (2021+, 150 units), quad-motor EV, single-speed, AWD torque vectoring, 120 kWh structural battery. 1914 PS / 1408 kW combined (verified), curb weight 2150 kg (verified) — the only car here in the Chiron's power league, and nearly as heavy. The roster-wide 0.85 crank-to-wheel factor overstates EV drivetrain loss a little (documented convention in cars.ts). cdA is an estimate (~0.30 Cd x ~2.2 m2 frontal area). Michelin Pilot Sport 4S tyres; four-motor torque vectoring gives the best launch traction in the roster (1.85 s 0-60, verified) and makes it the most computer-managed, forgiving car at speed — hence the roster-lowest errorSigma. vMax is the 352 km/h customer-car electronic limit; the 412 km/h record run (verified) required a special unlocked event. Like the Chiron, a 2.15-tonne hypercar isn't flung through tight corners — muLat and aggression kept conservative; its weapons are launch, torque-fill out of corners, and the straights. Aggression sits below even the Chiron's: unlike every other car here, its grip-limited acceleration reaches the cornering limit of a twisty approach road, and a driver leaning on that limit in a 2.15 t car has no braking margin left (empirically it repeatedly ran the first-hairpin trap on petropolis-teresopolis at aggression 0.94; 0.90 races cleanly). Peak-power road speed left at the floor default — full torque from a standstill. Speed-limit tolerance (R10, a driver trait like aggression — not a spec) set low for a hypercar: conspicuous and very valuable, so driven closer to the signs than a hot hatch. Kept separate from aggression precisely so this caution costs straight-line pace without also being cornering timidity.
